subject: Re: Follow-up: Rate limits, burst usage & overage terms
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Jul 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up & quick pricing questions from today's call

Alex — really enjoyed the demo and the deep dive with your ML and infra teams today. Per our conversation, I wanted to capture a short recap and a couple of clarifying questions so we can put together a concrete proposal.

Recap (high level):
- Primary use: customer support summarization + real-time agent assist for web and mobile chat.
- Expected avg request length: ~250 tokens input / ~150 tokens output.
- Current pilot: 150k active users with 50k weekly active users.
- Desired SLA: sub-300ms p99 for common flows.

Open questions for pricing/limits:
1) Can you confirm expected monthly token volume (avg and peak)? On the call you mentioned ~20M tokens/day during promos — is that a sustained peak or a short burst window?
2) For burst events (marketing promos), what's the maximum concurrent requests / estimated qps we should design for?
3) Do you have a target unit cost you want us to hit (roughly $/1M tokens) so we can shape options (batching, quantization, dedicated pool)?

Next steps: if you can reply with the numbers above I will:
- Draft two options: hosted with overage pricing + burst quota; and a Dedicated reserved-capacity proposal with committed throughput and lower unit economics.
- Include explicit overage terms and quota increase SLAs.

Attaching a high-level pricing summary for reference — I'll refine once we have the numbers.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0142
redwoodinference.com

Attachment: redwood_pricing_summary.pdf (one-page summary: hosted vs dedicated, sample $/1M token math)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmecorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acmecorp.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Jul 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up & quick pricing questions from today's call

Thanks Marissa — great meeting. Answers inline below.

1) Monthly token volume: baseline is ~300M tokens/month today. During product promos we see spikes up to ~20M tokens/day for 3–5 days. The peak weeks are typically 2x the baseline but concentrated in short windows.

2) Burst events: concurrent qps during promos has hit ~450 qps for the chat endpoint (short bursts up to ~10 minutes). For safety planning, design for up to 600 qps for 15-minute windows.

3) Target unit cost: our finance team wants to get to ~ $900–1,200 per 1M tokens (effective cost to us after discounts). If you can show an option close to $1,000 / 1M tokens at committed volume, that looks promising.

Also cc'd procurement — procurement will need to see overage caps, notification windows, and an SLA for quota increases (we typically require 24–48h ramp for guaranteed increases; for emergency burst support we may be able to accept higher overage rates).

Happy to sync if you want to run numbers together.

—Alex
Alex Johnson, Head of ML Product
Acme Corp
alex.johnson@acmecorp.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@acmecorp.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Jul 2027 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up & quick pricing questions from today's call

Appreciate the detail Alex — that helps a lot. Quick thoughts and proposed options:

Option A — Hosted (flexible, fast start):
- Baseline commit: 300M tokens/month at $1,200 / 1M tokens (list).
- Burst window: automatic burst pool up to +50% of baseline with short-term crediting; sustained bursts beyond that trigger overage pricing.
- Overage: $2,000 / 1M tokens for uncommitted overage; we can cap monthly overage to a negotiated amount to limit surprises.
- Quota increases: standard request SLA 48h; expedited 4–8h for emergency (subject to capacity).

Option B — Dedicated (best unit economics for sustained high volume):
- Reserved capacity nodes sized for expected baseline with headroom for 2x typical baseline.
- Effective unit cost: ~ $950 / 1M tokens at the 300M commit (quantized model path + batching).
- Burst handling: dedicated pool supports short bursts; for very large, seamless fallback to hosted pool with peered routing (falls back to $1,100 / 1M for overflow).
- Quota increases: SLA 24h for scaling reservations; immediate emergency scale via support for an additional fee.

We can also present a blended option: a short committed baseline with a cheaper overage cap (e.g., commit 200M, dedicated for baseline, hosted overflow).

Next steps:
- Rafael is looping in procurement language and overage clause templates for the hosted/dedicated options.
- If you confirm target budget (~$1,000 / 1M tokens) and acceptable burst cap behavior (e.g., allow hosted overflow at blended rate), I will put together a formal proposal and a sample SOW.

Posting the pricing summary we discussed — attached.

Cheers,
Marissa

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Procurement Team <procurement@acmecorp.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmecorp.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Jul 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up & quick pricing questions from today's call

Hi procurement — Rafael from Redwood here. Quick note on overage terms & quota increases so your legal/procurement team has a starting point: 

- Notification: Redwood will send automated usage alerts at 70%, 85%, and 95% of committed monthly tokens.
- Overage charges: standard hosted overage = $2,000 / 1M tokens; we can negotiate stepped overage tiers for larger bursts (e.g., $1,500 / 1M for the first 50M of overage if contracted).
- Burst protection: customers on Dedicated may purchase a "burst buffer" (short-term reserved slots) that guarantees capacity for X minutes; pricing is a one-time monthly fee based on requested concurrent capacity.
- Quota increase SLA: standard 48h for increases; 24h for committed customers; 4–8h expedited for emergency support (subject to capacity & fee).
- Cap clause: we can include a hard cap to stop usage past a negotiated overage threshold to prevent unexpected spend.

I'll attach a redlined clause for procurement if that helps — and happy to jump on a call to walk through.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmecorp.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Jul 2027 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up & quick pricing questions from today's call

Alex — quick operational note from the onboarding/ops side: if you go Dedicated + overflow, we recommend the following setup to hit the $1k / 1M target while meeting p99 latency: 

- Use a quantized model variant for lower unit cost on non-critical traffic (70% of calls), and keep a full-precision variant for high-quality/rare flows.
- Enable prefix and KV caching for common prompts to reduce token consumption by ~10–15%.
- Set up a burst buffer sized for ~500 qps for marketing promos (matches what you asked for) with an automated fallback policy to hosted overflow once buffer is exhausted.

I'll work with Rafael on the exact sizing math and include it in the proposal. If procurement can share any maximum allowable overage cap (monthly $ or %), we can finalize the clause and pricing.

Thanks — Camila
 Senior Customer Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com
